## TL;DR

Addressed both findings from review round 1. The mobile architecture document now points readers to ADR 0011 for the connected-server screen direction and explains which Capacitor host responsibilities remain in force. I also cleared the stale `needs_input` flags on follow-up tasks #1112–#1116 through RepoOS after confirming their sections were already present. The work remains documentation and task planning only; it does not change application behavior.

## Work and rationale

The acceptance criteria asked for both `mobile-ux-strategy.md` and `mobile-architecture.md` to record the new direction and link the ADR. The first review found that only the strategy document and ADR were in the branch diff. I reviewed the start of `docs/mobile-architecture.md` and added a callout immediately below its title so the changed direction is visible before readers encounter the older host-architecture material.

The callout says ADR 0011 supersedes the native screen-composition direction for connected-server screens. It links directly to the ADR and states that the server-served SPA provides the narrow-screen composition in browsers and in the host WebView. It also defines the remaining scope of the older document: Capacitor still handles server selection, the lock screen, and the isolated WebView security boundary, and the compatibility findings remain applicable. This wording keeps the architecture document useful while making the relationship between the two decisions explicit.

The second review finding concerned metadata on #1112 through #1116. The review observed that each task has Problem, Desired UX, Acceptance criteria, and Notes for AI sections, while its frontmatter still said those last two sections were missing. I checked the branch copy and confirmed those follow-up task files are not present there; they live on the RepoOS board. I therefore used `repoos update <id> --needs-input false` for each task, as required for task metadata, instead of editing task files directly. RepoOS confirmed each update. This resolves the stale flag without changing the task specifications or their statuses.

No application code was changed. The previous round had already confirmed that the ADR, strategy update, and follow-up task split matched the intended direction. The new changes are limited to closing the two specific documentation and metadata gaps.

## Approaches tried

I first read the full round 1 review report and the live task state. The report identified the exact missing document callout and the affected follow-up task IDs. I then attempted the normal work-in-progress inspection sequence; the CLI reported that the task had already returned to `review`, which is why I used `repoos mv 1110 active` before editing. RepoOS moved it back to active.

For the architecture document I chose a short, high-visibility callout rather than rewriting the older document. Its original content records the Capacitor host security and compatibility work, which ADR 0011 explicitly retains. Replacing that content would have obscured still-valid findings and broadened the change beyond the review request.

For task metadata I chose the supported `repoos update` command, setting `needs_input` to false on each of the five follow-ups. The section-completeness evidence was the task content referenced in the review report and the fact that the follow-ups had already been filed as complete specifications.

## Challenges and blockers

The prior handoff message reported that the task had no registered worktree for its branch. The live board showed #1110 in review, and the worktree had no advisory lock file. I returned it to active through RepoOS before making changes, following the repository's review-state rule. A fresh handoff request is still needed after the scoped check so RepoOS can retry its managed registration and commit steps.

The first `repoos list` invocation detected a stale local build and began rebuilding it. I allowed that command to complete before continuing. The required `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` then completed successfully. Since the diff was classified as docs/bookkeeping-only, the plan skipped build, lint, tests, and UI smoke; formatting, lockfile/runtime-dependency guards, branch-artifact and task-asset checks, and task parsing passed. This records the scoped check result accurately without implying that skipped steps ran.

## Key learnings

The mobile direction has two distinct layers: the browser-facing connected-server composition and the native host that selects and isolates a server. Clear supersession language should name the layer being replaced and identify the host responsibilities that remain, so readers do not interpret a UX change as invalidating the security boundary.

RepoOS follow-up specs and their metadata are separate sources of truth. If a review finds a stale metadata flag on tasks outside the feature branch, the correct repair is through the RepoOS command/API, not by copying or editing those task files in the branch. The same check should look across every task in the reported class, which in this case meant all five follow-ups.
